**1. Where should refund provider calls live, and does the code follow that pattern today?**

New refund calls should live in `medibill/backend/app/billing/gateway.py`, as a new accessor (e.g. `refund(...)`) alongside the existing `charge()` (gateway.py:11–13) and `create_customer()` (gateway.py:16–17), using the module-level client built at gateway.py:8. That is the pattern the repository declares in two places: `medibill/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:5–7` ("Every call to the payment provider goes through app/billing/gateway.py; the only exception is app/billing/errors.py") and the gateway's own docstring, gateway.py:1–5 ("This module is the single place the chargekit provider client is built").

The code does **not** follow that pattern everywhere today. A case-insensitive grep for `chargekit` across the whole medibill tree, plus a grep for `requests|httpx|urllib|http` (no matches, so the SDK is the only channel to the provider), gives the complete list:

- `medibill/backend/app/api/invoices.py` — **violation.** Imports the SDK at line 4, constructs its own `chargekit.Client(api_key_env="CHARGEKIT_API_KEY")` at line 14, and calls `client.charge(...)` directly at lines 15–16 inside the `POST /invoices/{invoice_id}/charge` route. `git show 23d2f37:backend/app/api/invoices.py` shows this direct call has existed since the initial commit (MEDB-180) — the same commit that introduced the doc claiming the boundary.
- `medibill/backend/app/workers/dunning.py` — **violation.** Imports the SDK at line 2 and constructs a fresh `chargekit.Client(...).charge(...)` per overdue invoice at lines 9–13. Added in commit `3a7daee` (MEDB-197), which touched only this file — the doc's "only exception" sentence was already false the day this landed.
- `medibill/backend/app/billing/errors.py:6` — **not a violation.** Imports only `chargekit.errors` (error classes `ChargeDeclined`, `ProviderUnavailable`), which is exactly the exception the doc names.
- `medibill/backend/app/billing/gateway.py` — the boundary module itself.
- `medibill/README.md:4` — prose mention only.

So there are exactly two places that talk to the provider "some other way," both by constructing their own SDK client instead of calling gateway accessors: `api/invoices.py` and `workers/dunning.py`.

**2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` versus the actual code.**

All three sections of the document are contradicted by the code in specific ways:

- *Payment integration* (ARCHITECTURE.md:5–7): claims every provider call goes through `app/billing/gateway.py` with `app/billing/errors.py` as the only exception. In reality, `api/invoices.py:14–16` and `workers/dunning.py:9–13` call the provider directly with their own clients (details in answer 1). The invoices.py deviation has existed since the same commit that wrote the doc; the dunning.py one was added later without touching the doc.
- *Invoice API* (ARCHITECTURE.md:11–12): claims the response contains "exactly the fields: id, tenant_id, amount_cents, currency, status." The actual response model `InvoiceOut` (`medibill/backend/app/models/invoice.py:16–22`) has a sixth field, `external_ref` (line 22), populated by `from_model` (line 28) and returned by the charge endpoint (`api/invoices.py:17–18`). The backing column was added by `backend/migrations/0006_add_invoice_external_ref.sql`. Git shows the field was added in commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214, "record external payment ref on invoices"), whose `--stat` includes four code files and no doc change — the doc described the wire shape correctly as of migration 0001 and went stale at MEDB-214.
- *Webhooks* (ARCHITECTURE.md:16–17): claims the integration handles 4 event types (payment_succeeded, payment_failed, refund_created, dispute_opened). The handler `payment_webhook` (`backend/app/api/webhooks.py:8–20`) handles five: it also recognizes `payment_pending` (webhooks.py:14–15), added in the same MEDB-214 commit, again with no doc update. Unrecognized types are accepted and return `{"handled": None}` (webhooks.py:20), a behavior the doc doesn't mention at all.

In short, the doc was accurate for the invoice shape and webhook set at the initial commit and has not been touched since (`git log --stat` shows `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` only ever appears in `23d2f37`), while the boundary claim was inaccurate even at the moment it was written.

**3. What should happen to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and when?**

It should be brought back in line with reality **now, before any refund code is written** — drift between an architecture contract and the code is a bug to fix immediately, not a doc chore to schedule, and building refunds against a document that is wrong on all three of its sections invites the new code to copy the wrong pattern (a refund implementer imitating `api/invoices.py` would inline another `chargekit.Client`). Concretely:

- Preferably, restore the boundary invariant first: a small preparatory commit routing `api/invoices.py` and `workers/dunning.py` through gateway accessors, after which the doc's payment-integration section becomes true again. If that refactor is deferred, the doc must instead be edited to honestly list `api/invoices.py` and `workers/dunning.py` as current, known exceptions — an accurate exception list is more useful than a clean claim that grep disproves in seconds.
- Update the Invoice API section to include `external_ref`, or better, drop the "exactly these fields" enumeration and point at `InvoiceOut` in `backend/app/models/invoice.py` as the source of truth for the wire shape.
- Fix the webhook section as described in answer 4.
- Going forward — and this applies to the refund feature itself — any commit that changes what the doc governs (the provider boundary, the invoice response shape, the webhook set) must update `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` in that same commit, with the doc change called out in the commit/PR summary. The refund work will add at least a new gateway accessor and likely touch the API surface and webhook handling, so its PR must carry the doc update with it. Commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214) is the existing counterexample: it changed two documented contracts in one commit and never touched the doc.

**4. The webhook event-type claim.**

The claim at ARCHITECTURE.md:16–17 — "The integration handles 4 webhook event types: payment_succeeded, payment_failed, refund_created, dispute_opened" — is wrong on both the count and the list: `backend/app/api/webhooks.py:10–19` handles five types, the undocumented one being `payment_pending` (lines 14–15). It was correct when written (the initial commit's handler had exactly the four listed types) and drifted when MEDB-214 added the fifth branch without a doc edit.

Beyond correcting the content, I would change **how** it is stated: remove the hardcoded count entirely. A literal "4" is the kind of fact that is guaranteed to rot — it already has once, and the refund feature is likely to touch this exact list again (e.g. a `refund_failed` event), which would re-stale a corrected "5" immediately. Restate it as a property plus a pointer to the single source of truth, something like: "Webhook events are dispatched in `backend/app/api/webhooks.py::payment_webhook`; the handled event types are exactly the ones matched there, and unrecognized types are accepted with `{"handled": null}`." If an inline list is kept for reader convenience, it should carry no count and an explicit note that it changes in the same commit as the handler. One caveat on the word "handles": every branch in the current handler is an acknowledgment stub that returns a label and performs no side effects, so even a corrected sentence overstates what the integration does — worth wording as "recognizes/accepts" until real processing exists.

So there are exactly two places that talk to the provider "some other way," both by constructing their own SDK client instead of calling gateway accessors: `api/invoices.py` and `workers/dunning.py`.

**2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` versus the actual code.**

All three sections of the document are contradicted by the code in specific ways:

- *Payment integration* (ARCHITECTURE.md:5–7): claims every provider call goes through `app/billing/gateway.py` with `app/billing/errors.py` as the only exception. In reality, `api/invoices.py:14–16` and `workers/dunning.py:9–13` call the provider directly with their own clients (details in answer 1). The invoices.py deviation has existed since the same commit that wrote the doc; the dunning.py one was added later without touching the doc.
- *Invoice API* (ARCHITECTURE.md:11–12): claims the response contains "exactly the fields: id, tenant_id, amount_cents, currency, status." The actual response model `InvoiceOut` (`medibill/backend/app/models/invoice.py:16–22`) has a sixth field, `external_ref` (line 22), populated by `from_model` (line 28) and returned by the charge endpoint (`api/invoices.py:17–18`). The backing column was added by `backend/migrations/0006_add_invoice_external_ref.sql`. Git shows the field was added in commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214, "record external payment ref on invoices"), whose `--stat` includes four code files and no doc change — the doc described the wire shape correctly as of migration 0001 and went stale at MEDB-214.
- *Webhooks* (ARCHITECTURE.md:16–17): claims the integration handles 4 event types (payment_succeeded, payment_failed, refund_created, dispute_opened). The handler `payment_webhook` (`backend/app/api/webhooks.py:8–20`) handles five: it also recognizes `payment_pending` (webhooks.py:14–15), added in the same MEDB-214 commit, again with no doc update. Unrecognized types are accepted and return `{"handled": None}` (webhooks.py:20), a behavior the doc doesn't mention at all.

In short, the doc was accurate for the invoice shape and webhook set at the initial commit and has not been touched since (`git log --stat` shows `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` only ever appears in `23d2f37`), while the boundary claim was inaccurate even at the moment it was written.

**3. What should happen to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and when?**

It should be brought back in line with reality **now, before any refund code is written** — drift between an architecture contract and the code is a bug to fix immediately, not a doc chore to schedule, and building refunds against a document that is wrong on all three of its sections invites the new code to copy the wrong pattern (a refund implementer imitating `api/invoices.py` would inline another `chargekit.Client`). Concretely:

- Preferably, restore the boundary invariant first: a small preparatory commit routing `api/invoices.py` and `workers/dunning.py` through gateway accessors, after which the doc's payment-integration section becomes true again. If that refactor is deferred, the doc must instead be edited to honestly list `api/invoices.py` and `workers/dunning.py` as current, known exceptions — an accurate exception list is more useful than a clean claim that grep disproves in seconds.
- Update the Invoice API section to include `external_ref`, or better, drop the "exactly these fields" enumeration and point at `InvoiceOut` in `backend/app/models/invoice.py` as the source of truth for the wire shape.
- Fix the webhook section as described in answer 4.
- Going forward — and this applies to the refund feature itself — any commit that changes what the doc governs (the provider boundary, the invoice response shape, the webhook set) must update `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` in that same commit, with the doc change called out in the commit/PR summary. The refund work will add at least a new gateway accessor and likely touch the API surface and webhook handling, so its PR must carry the doc update with it. Commit `c23da88` (MEDB-214) is the existing counterexample: it changed two documented contracts in one commit and never touched the doc.

**4. The webhook event-type claim.**

The claim at ARCHITECTURE.md:16–17 — "The integration handles 4 webhook event types: payment_succeeded, payment_failed, refund_created, dispute_opened" — is wrong on both the count and the list: `backend/app/api/webhooks.py:10–19` handles five types, the undocumented one being `payment_pending` (lines 14–15). It was correct when written (the initial commit's handler had exactly the four listed types) and drifted when MEDB-214 added the fifth branch without a doc edit.

Beyond correcting the content, I would change **how** it is stated: remove the hardcoded count entirely. A literal "4" is the kind of fact that is guaranteed to rot — it already has once, and the refund feature is likely to touch this exact list again (e.g. a `refund_failed` event), which would re-stale a corrected "5" immediately. Restate it as a property plus a pointer to the single source of truth, something like: "Webhook events are dispatched in `backend/app/api/webhooks.py::payment_webhook`; the handled event types are exactly the ones matched there, and unrecognized types are accepted with `{"handled": null}`." If an inline list is kept for reader convenience, it should carry no count and an explicit note that it changes in the same commit as the handler. One caveat on the word "handles": every branch in the current handler is an acknowledgment stub that returns a label and performs no side effects, so even a corrected sentence overstates what the integration does — worth wording as "recognizes/accepts" until real processing exists.
